necessary_context.content: For integer d>=1 and real T>=0, F_d(T)={f in C²(R^d): inf f>−infinity, f(0)−inf f<=T, Lip(Hessian f)<=1}. Vector norms are Euclidean and matrix norms are operator norms. Ordinary queries return (f,gradient f); rich queries return (f,gradient f,Hessian f). G and H are separate hard caps; rich calls are not charged to G. No gradient-Lipschitz or Hessian-norm bound is imposed.
necessary_context.name: Normalized class and oracle

necessary_context.applies_to: Main envelope and its scaling transfer
necessary_context.content: Policies, query choices and outputs are measurable; the private seed is independent of the fixed input. Arbitrary exact-real queries and possibly unqueried outputs are allowed. Success means gradient norm <=1 with probability >=2/3 separately on every fixed legal input. Internal computation is free, consists of measurable steps, and terminates at a measurable finite time on every legal input without a uniform running-time bound. Finite parameter-dependent advice independent of the unknown input is allowed. Query caps hold on every execution and are enforced on counterfactual histories by stopping before an excess query; proof simulations use a finite computation cutoff removed under the legal input law.
necessary_context.name: Algorithm and success conventions

necessary_context.content: Theorem 3.2 uses finite hierarchy depth L and n=8^L, unrelated to Hessian-Lipschitz scale L2. M=1+4096J², J integer>=J0; each leaf contains M sequential marked tasks. The main matching theorem requires h>=1 even though the parameter theorem permits h=0.
necessary_context.name: Hierarchy notation
